## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update, fused with a direct framebuffer scatter, can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 9.198 ns/p at N=4000 to 6.528 at N=16000 — overhead amortization below and around the L1d spill (N≈963). Past the L2 spill (N≈61680), cost stays FLAT: 6.396 ns/p at N=65000, 6.378 at N=262000, then rises gently to 6.749 at N=1M and 6.941 at N=4M — no sharp DRAM knee. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: the flat region moves from ~6.4 ns/p (q=0.01) to ~7.0 (q=0.05), ~7.8 (q=0.1), ~9.9 (q=0.25), and ~13.6 (q=0.5), but the amortize-then-flat-then-gentle-rise N-shape is preserved across all death rates.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 10.66 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 42% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound at small N (7.39 GB/s at N=4000) and settles into a bandwidth-limited regime by N=16000 that never exceeds 10.6 GB/s. Death rate drives the transition: bandwidth holds ~10.6 GB/s at q=0.01, drops to ~9.7 at q=0.05, ~8.7 at q=0.1, ~6.8 at q=0.25, and ~5.0 at q=0.5. The algo never approaches the streaming ceiling; the fused scatter's extra framebuffer traffic and branchy respawn cost keep it at 42% even in the best case.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized walk1 across the components of a single particle: `ldur q7` loads 16 bytes, `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` rearranges components, `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` do 4-wide single-precision math, and `stur q6` writes back. A `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x10]` is an indexed element load — a mini-gather for one component. Walk2 (the fused scatter) is entirely scalar: 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` for byte-granular framebuffer read-modify-write, 18 `csel` for 0–255 clamping, and a `bl _layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn` call per respawn. The component-wise vectorization in walk1 explains the steady 10.6 GB/s floor, but the scatter's byte stores — `strb w16, [x15]`, `strb w24, [x23, x14]` — cap bandwidth at 42% of ceiling, and the branch-heavy scatter/respawn logic (20 `cmp`, 19 `b`) explains the death-rate sensitivity.

## Verdict
Partially — walk1 auto-vectorizes with `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` and the N-curve shows no cache-spill knee, but the fused scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes cap achieved bandwidth at 10.66 GB/s = 42% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling even at q=0.01, and branchy respawn drives it to 5.0 GB/s (20% of ceiling) by q=0.5. The hypothesis holds only in the sense that autovec produces stable, cache-resilient throughput; it does not approach the streaming ceiling in any regime.
